Let us go: *gacche*, *gacchāmase*. In the causative (*ghammādese*): let him cause to go: *ghammatu*, *ghammantu*, etc. In the passive (*kammani*): let he be caused to go:
*gacchīyataṃ*, *gacchīyatu*; let he be caused to go: *gamīyataṃ*, *gamīyatu*; let he be gone to: *gammataṃ*, *gammatu*, etc.
In the case of a formal injunction (*vidhi*), it is as follows: "Let there be a mountain here; let this palace be made of gold," and so forth.
In the case of an invitation (*nimantana*): "Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One accept my meal; may your honor sit here. In the case of a request (*ajjhesana*):
"Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One teach the Dhamma."
"May your honor ask a question regarding the *anumati*; may your honor enter; may your honor sit here.
'Patthanā' means a request: 'Grant me five excellent villages; give me one eye. 'The time has arrived for you;
it is the time for you to perform the *kaṭa* (deed); may your honor perform the *kaṭa*,' and so forth."
The Fifth Case Ending (Pañcamīvibhatti).
453. *eyya*, *eyyuṃ*; *eyyāsi*, *eyyātha*; *eyyāmi*, *eyyāma*; *etha*, *eraṃ*; *etho*, *eyyāvho*; *eyyaṃ*, *eyyāmhe*.
These twelve, beginning with *eyya*, are known as the seventh case endings (*sattamī*).
The term “anuttakāle” (at a time other than when stated) is understood [to apply here]. 454. The seventh case ending occurs in the senses of *anumati* (consent) and *parikappa* (supposition).
In the sense of consent and in the sense of supposition, the seventh case ending occurs at a time other than when explicitly stated.

By the inclusion of the word *attha*, the locative case is used in contexts such as injunctions (*vidhi*) and invitations (*nimantana*). *Anumati* is the granting of permission by another to one who desires to act.

*Parikappa* is a supposition; it is an observation or examination in the form of "if indeed it were so," and it also refers to the supposition of the occurrence of a resultant action based on the occurrence of a causal action.
In that context, according to the alternative formulation (*parikappa*), the seventh case, the second person singular, and the first person singular endings would be *-eyya*.

The absence of suffixes, vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*), and so forth, would be the same as in the preceding [forms]. By the rule "in some cases the verbal root replaces the inflection" (*kvaci dhātu vibhatti*), there is the substitution of the vowel *e* for these forms: *-eyya*, *-eyyāsi*, *-eyyāmi*, and *-eyyaṃ*.
Now, what indeed would happen? If he were to go forth in his first stage of life, he would become an Arahant.
If volitional formations were permanent, they would not cease. If you were to exist, you all would exist.
How could I become a deva? What indeed could we become? One might exist; one might come to be.
You two might exist; you two might come to be.
In the optative mood (*patthana*), however: "May I be happy," *bhaveyyam*; "may I become," *bhaveyyam* or *bhaveyyāmhe*. "May happiness be experienced by you," *anubhūyetha*;
"may it be experienced [by us]," *anubhūyeraṃ*. "May it be experienced by you two," *anubhūyetho*; "may it be experienced by you both," *anubhūyeyyāvho*.

"May it be experienced by me," *anubhūye*, *anubhūyeyyam*, or *anubhūyeyyāmhe*. In the third-person form (*parassapada*): "may he experience," *anubhūyeyya*; "may they experience," *anubhūyeyyuṃ*. "May you experience," *anubhūyeyyāsi*.
And so forth. In the sense of state (*bhāve*), it would be *bhūyetha*.
In the sense of injunction (*vidhimhi*): he would cook the rice—*pace*, *paceyya*, *paceyyuṃ*; you (singular) cook—*pace*, *paceyyāsi*, you (plural) would cook—*paceyyātha*;

I cook—*pace*, I would cook—*paceyyāmi*, we would cook—*paceyyāma*; may you (plural) cook—*pacetha*, may they cook—*paceyuṃ*; may you two cook—*pacetho*, may you two cook—*paceyyāvho*; may you (singular) cook—*pace*.

*Paceyyaṃ*, *paceyyāmhe*. In the passive (kamma), *paccetha*, *pacceraṃ*. *Paccetho*, *pacceyyāvho*. *Pacce*, *paceyyaṃ*, *paceyyāmhe*. When the parassapada endings are used: *pacce*, *pacceyya*, *pacceyyuṃ*; *paceyyāsi*, etc. In the sense of permission:
*so gāmaṃ gacche*, *gaccheyya*; or, by the rule "kvaci dhātū" and so forth, the *eyya* suffix may optionally become *uṃ*, thus *gacchuṃ*.
They might go. You might go; you might go (plural). I might go; we might go. He might go; they might go.
He might go; you might go (plural); you might go (singular).
I might go; we might go. You two might go; you two might go (plural). I might go; we two might go; we all might go.
In the imperative mood: *gametha*, *gameraṃ*, and so forth. In the passive voice (*kamma-kāraka*):

*gacchīyetha*, *gamīyetha*, *gacchīyeraṃ*, *gamīyeraṃ*, and so forth. In the parassapada (active) voice: *gacchīyeyya*, *gamīyeyya*, *gammeyya*, *gammeyyuṃ*, and so forth. Likewise in the optative mood (*ghamme*): *ghammeyya*, *ghammeyyuṃ*, and so forth. This concludes the seventh case ending (the imperative).
The method of analysis for the temporal classification of the present negative construction.
455. *Āu*, *ottha*, *aṃhā*, *tthatthuṃ*, *sevhaṃ*, *iṃmhase*—these twelve, beginning with *ā*, are designated as the past tense (*hiyyattanī*).
The terms "not perceptible" (appaccakkhe) and "past" (atīte) are understood [to apply here].
456. Regarding the "yesterday-tense" (hiyyattanī):

when the time is past, starting from yesterday, whether it be perceptible or not perceptible, the *hiyyattanī* case-ending occurs; thus, the first person singular of the *hiyyattanī* parasmaipada is *ā*.
The phrase “in some cases” (*kvaci*) from the beginning [of the previous rule] and “of roots” (*dhātūnaṃ*) from the current rule continue [into this one].
457. An augment *a* occurs before the initial [consonant] of roots in the third person singular past tense (*hiyyattanī*), the present tense (*ajjatanī*), and the future tense (*kālātipatti*).

That is to say, an augment *a* is inserted at the beginning of roots in these three case-endings: the third person singular past, the present, and the future. If it is asked, “How is it that this augment *a* occurs at the beginning of the root? [the answer follows].
Even when there is a suffix beginning with *s*, this [augment] occurs after the end of a verbal root, provided that the letter *k* follows again;
because it would otherwise be purposeless, it is placed at the beginning of the root to avoid obstructing the grammatical operation.
The rules regarding the absence of suffixes, vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*), the substitution of *ava*, and the elision of *sa-ra* and so forth follow the same method already stated.

*Abhavā*, *abhavuṃ*. *Abhavo*: by the rule "in some cases [the suffix] *dhātu*," etc., there is optionally the substitution of *a* for the vowel *o*; thus, *abhava*, *abhavattha*. *Abhavaṃ*, *abhavamhā*. *Abhavattha*, *abhavatthuṃ*. *Abhavase*, *abhavavhaṃ*. *Abhaviṃ*, *abhavamhase*. In the passive voice (*kammani*), the suffix *ya* is applied:
*tayā sukham anvabhūyattha*. In the absence of the augment *a*, it is *anubhūyattha*.
By the rule "in some cases [the suffix] *dhātu*," etc., there is the substitution of *th* for *tth*; thus, *anvabhūyatha*, *anubhūyatha*, *anvabhūyatthuṃ*, *anubhūyatthuṃ*.
*Anvabhūyase*, *anubhūyase*, *anvabhūyavhaṃ*, *anubhūyavhaṃ*. *Anvabhūyiṃ*, *anubhūyiṃ*, *anvabhūyamhase*, *anubhūyamhase*.
In the parassapada (active voice), *anvabhūyā*, *anubhūyā*, and so forth. In the bhāve (passive/impersonal), *anvabhūyattha*. Likewise:
he cooked the rice—*apacā*, *pacā*, *apacū*, *pacū*. *Apaco*, *paco*, *apacattha*, *pacattha*. *Apacaṃ*.
*Pacaṃ*, *apacamhā*, *pacamhā*. *Apacattha*, *pacattha*, *apacatthu*, *pacatthuṃ*.
*Apacase*, *pacase*, *apacavhaṃ*, *pacavhaṃ*. *Apaciṃ*, *paciṃ*, *apacamhase*, *pacamhase*.
In the passive (*kammani*): *apaccatha*, *apaccattha*, *apaccatthuṃ*. *Apaccase*, *apaccavhaṃ*. *Apacciṃ*, *apaccamhase*. *Apaccā*, *apaccū*, and so forth.
Likewise: *agaccha*, *agacchu*; *agaccho*, *agaccha*, *agacchattha*; *agacchaṃ*, *agacchamhā*; *agacchattha*, *agacchatthuṃ*;
*agacchase*, *agacchavhaṃ*; *agacchiṃ*, *agacchamhase*. *agamā*, *agamū*; *agamo*, *agama*, *agamattha*;
*agamaṃ*, *agamamhā*; *agamattha*, *agamatthuṃ*; *agamase*, *agamavhaṃ*; *agamiṃ*, *agamamhase*.

In the *kamma* (object) case: *agacchīyattha*, *gacchīyattha*, *agamīyattha*, *gamīyattha*, *agacchīyatthuṃ*, *gacchīyatthuṃ*, *agamīyatthuṃ*, *gamīyatthuṃ*, and so forth. Likewise: *aghammā*, *aghammū*, and so forth. This is the *hiyyattanī* (past tense) inflection.
458. The *hiyyattanī*, *sattamī* (aorist), *pañcamī* (future), and *vattamānā* (present) [inflections] apply to all verbal roots (*sabbadhātuka*).

The four case endings beginning with *hiyyattanā* (the past tense) are designated as *sabbadhātuka*. Because the endings beginning with *hiyyattanā* are designated as *sabbadhātuka*, the augment *i*—which is prescribed by the rule "the augment *i* occurs before a non-*sabbadhātuka*" (*ikārāgamo asabbadhātukamhī*)—does not occur.
[These endings are] *sabbadhātuka*.
459. The *parokkhā* (aorist) endings are: *a*, *u*, *e*, *ttha*, *aṃ*, *mha*, *ttha*, *re*, *tho*, *vho*, *iṃ*, *mhe*.

The twelve beginning with *a* are known as the "remote" (*parokkhā*) tenses. Because they indicate what is beyond the range of the sense organs (*akkhānaṃ indriyānaṃ paraṃ*), this grammatical case is called "remote.
460. *Apaccakkhe parokkhātīte*:

When the subject is not present—that is, when it has become an object outside the range of the sense organs—and refers to past time, the remote tense occurs. It is called "past" (*atīta*) because it has passed away (*atikkamma ito*); the meaning is that it has passed after having existed.
According to the method stated below, the third person singular of the aorist (parokkhā) in the parassapada voice is *a*.

Here, in the rule "bhū a," by way of transformation (*vipariṇāmena*), the term "of roots" (*dhātūnam*) is understood from the preceding context. 461. In certain instances, there is doubling of single vowels that are initial sounds.

In certain instances, there is a doubling of the initial consonant of verbal roots that consist of a single vowel. The word "in certain instances" (*kvaci*) here has the sense of a fixed distribution (*vavatthita-vibhāsa*). Therefore:
"In the case of the *parokkhā* (past tense) suffix, there is doubling of all roots after the letters *kha*, *cha*, and *sa*;
likewise, in the case of suffixes lacking a prefix (*appaccaya*), such as *juhotyādi*, there is doubling in certain instances within the *kicca* and other grammatical operations."
“Bhū bhū a”—this is *pubbobbhāsa* (repetition of the first part).
That which is the first constituent of a doubled element is designated as *abbhāsa*; thus, it is called the *abbhāsa-saññā* (designation of the repetition).
The inclusion of "nearby" (abbhāsa) follows. 463.

"Or the vowel *i* and the vowel *a* [are substituted] for the interior of a nearby sound. For the interior of a nearby sound, there is either the vowel *i* or the vowel *a*. This word "or" (*vā*) has the sense of a fixed alternative (*vavatthitavibhāsa*). Therefore—
The letter *i* [is substituted] for a vowel following *kha*, *cha*, *sa*, or *su*;
*ī* [is substituted] for a vowel followed by *guṇa* after *ikāra*; and optionally, [the substitution of *ī* occurs] for the root *bhū* in the *parokkhā* tense.
"Akāra does not [arise] from another. This means that the letter *a* replaces the letter *ū*. 464.
For the second and fourth [consonants], the first and third [vowels] [are substituted].

For the second and fourth groups of consonants (*vagga*) that have reached the *abbhāsa* (the preceding vowel), the first and third [consonants] occur respectively; thus, the letter *bha* becomes *ba*.
465. *Brū-bhū-nam-āha-bhū-vā parokkhāyaṃ*.
For these roots, *brū* and *bhū*, the substitutes *āha* and *bhūva* respectively occur in the *parokkhā* (aorist) case ending; thus, for the word *bhūs*, [the substitute is *bhūva*].
There is the substitution of *bhū* [for *as*]. By the rule beginning with “*saralopo mādesappaccayādimhī*,” there is the elision of *sa*, etc. Thus: “That king, it is said, became (*babhūva*);
they, it is said, became (*babhūvu*); you, it is said, became (*babhūve*).
The term “from roots” (*dhātūhi*) is understood [from the previous rule], and there is also the occasional inclusion [of forms] by way of the lion’s gait (*sīhagati*).
466. The augment *i* occurs before a non-suffixal verbal root (*asabbadhātu*).
Whenever a non-suffixal verbal root follows, the augment *i* sometimes occurs after the roots.
When a non-suffixal root begins with a consonant, the augment *v* occurs.
In some cases [the suffix] occurs due to its governing function (*adhikāra*), and in some cases it may not occur even when [the condition for its application] exists.

And here, having defined "sabbadhātuka" as that which is not "asabbadhātuka," the past tense (*hiyyattanī*), the seventh (optative), the fifth (imperative), and the present (*vattamānā*) are designated as *sabbadhātuka* because they are stated with the technical name *sabbadhātuka*; therefore, the other four case-endings (*vibhatti*)—[namely, the first, second, third, and fourth]—are [excluded].
It is called "asabbadhātuka" (non-asabbadhātuka). [In the active voice:

*tumhe kira babhūvittha* (you, it is said, were); *ahaṃ kira babhūvaṃ* (I, it is said, was); *mayaṃ kira babhūvimha* (we, it is said, were). In the middle voice (*attanopada*): *babhūvittha*, *babhūvire*; *babhūvittho*, *babhūvivho*; *babhūviṃ*, *babhūvimhe*.

In the passive (*kammani*) middle voice, there is the addition of the vowel *ī* and the suffix *ya*, with the addition of the vowel *y*: *anubabhūvīyittha*, because the suffix *ya* occurs in a non-asabbadhātuka context.
When the elision (*lopa*) has been performed by the rule beginning with "kvaci dhātū," the augment *ivaṇṇa* does not occur;
thus, for example: *anubabhūvittha*, *anubabhūvire*, and so forth.

In the sense of the abstract state (*bhāva*), there are *babhūvīyittha* or *babhūvittha*. Likewise: *papaca*, *papacū*; *papace*, *papacittha*; *papacam*, *papacimha*; *papacittha*, *papacire*; *papacittho*, *papacivho*; *papacim*, *papacimhe*.
In *kammani*, there is the form *papaccittha* and *papaccire*, etc.; likewise, *apacca* and *apaccū*, etc.

In the case of the root *gam*, by the rule beginning with “kvacādivaṇṇānaṃ,” there is doubling (*dvebhāva*), and by the rule “pubbobbhāso,” it receives the technical designation *abbhāsa*. The term “in the presence of *abbhāsa*” (*abbhāse*) is understood to carry over [from the previous rule].
467. The *ca*-group [replaces] the *ka*-group.
When the *ka*-group occurs in proximity (*abbhāsa*), it becomes the *ca*-group; thus, the letter *va* becomes *ja*.

By the rule beginning with "In some cases, for verbal roots," there is a long vowel in the third-person singular of the present indicative (*paṭhamapurisekavacana*) when not in proximity. It is said that he went to the village (*jagāma*), or *jagama*, or *jagamu*.
Jagamā, jagamittha; jagamaṃ, jagamimha. Jagamittha, jagamire; jagamittho, jagamivho; jagamiṃ, jagamimhe. In the passive voice:
jagamīyittha, or jagamittha, and so forth.
This is the parokkhā (aorist) tense.
468. *Ajjatanī* (the present tense) has twelve endings: *ī*, *uṃ*, *o*, *ttha*, *iṃ*, *mhā*, *ā*, *ū*, *se*, *vhaṃ*, *amhe*.
These twelve, beginning with *ī*, are designated as *ajjatanī*. That which exists today (*ajja*) is called *ajjatana*; because it indicates this [time], this case-ending is called *ajjatanī*.
The terms "not in the presence of the speaker" (*apaccakkhe*), "in the past" (*atīte*), and "in the presence of the speaker" (*paccakkhe*) also carry over [from the previous rule].
469. *Ajjatanī* (the "today" suffix).

From today onwards, beginning from this very day, the *ajjatanī* case-suffix occurs for both past time and for the present and non-present [times]. Thus, the first person singular of the *parassapada* (active voice) for *ajjatanī* is *-ī*. As in the previous [rule], there is the augment *-a-* (*akārāgama*), as well as the *vuddhi* (vowel strengthening) and so forth.
By the rule "in some cases, the verbal root and the case-suffixes," etc., the case-suffixes such as *-ī*, *-mha*, and so on [are applied].

In some instances there is shortening, the substitution of *ittha* for the words *o* and *āva*, and the elision of *sa* and so forth; thus we have *so abhavi* or *abhavī*, and in the absence of the insertion of the vowel *a*, *bhavi*.
By the "frog's leap" (*maṇḍūkagati*), the word "optionally" (*vā*) carries over.
470. *Sabbato uṃ iṃ su*.
After all verbal roots (*dhātu*), the substitution of *iṃ* occurs optionally for the case ending *uṃ*.
They were: *te abhaviṃsu*, or *bhaviṃsu*; or *abhavuṃ*, or *bhavuṃ*. You were: *tvaṃ abhavi*, or *bhavi*; or *abhavo*, or *bhavo*.
Or, "you were," or "you became"—there is the addition of the vowel *i*. "I was," or "I became";
"we were," or "we became," "we were" (*abhavimha*), or "we became" (*bhavimha*), or "we were" (*abhavimhā*), or "we became" (*bhavimhā*). "He was," or "he became"; "they were," or "they became";

"they were" (*abhavū*), or "they became" (*bhavū*). "I was" (*abhavise*), or "I became" (*bhavise*); "we were" (*abhavivhaṃ*), or "we became" (*bhavivhaṃ*). "I was" (*abhavaṃ*), or "I became" (*bhavaṃ*).
Or: *abhava*, *bhava*; *abhavimhe*, *bhavimhe*.
In the passive (*kamma*), when the suffix *ya* is elided, there is the substitution of *vuddhi* (vowel strengthening) and *āv* (the augment *ā*), etc.:
*sukhaṃ tayā anubhavittha*, *anvabhūyittha*, or *anubhūyittha*, and so forth. In the active voice (*parassapada*), [the forms are]: *tayā anvabhūyi*, *anubhūyi*, *anvabhūyī*, *anubhūyī*.
Or: *anvabhūyiṃsu*, *anubhūyiṃsu*, *anvabhūyuṃ*, *anubhūyuṃ*. You experienced: *anvabhūyi*, *anubhūyi*;
you (plural) experienced: *anvabhūyittha*, *anubhūyittha*. I experienced: *anvabhūyiṃ*, *anubhūyiṃ*; we experienced:
*anvabhūyimha*, *anubhūyimha*, or *anvabhūyimhā*, *anubhūyimhā*. In the passive voice: *abhavittha*, *abhūyittha* by you.
Thus: *apaci*, *paci*, *apacī*, or *pacī*; they [plural] were *apaciṃsu*, *paciṃsu*, *apacuṃ*, or *pacuṃ*.
You were *apaci*, *paci*, *apaco*, or *paco*; you [plural] were *apacittha* or *pacittha*. I was *apaciṃ*, *paciṃ*;
we [plural] were *apacimha*, *pacimha*, *apacimhā*, or *pacimhā*. He [singular] was *apacittha*, *pacittha*, *apacā*, or *pacā*; he [plural] was *apacū* or *pacū*.
Apacise, apacivhaṃ. Apacaṃ, pacaṃ, apaca, paca vā, apacimhe, pacimhe.
In the passive (kamma), *apaccittha*, *paccittha*, etc. In the parassapada (active) voice:
*apacci*, *pacci*, *apaccī*, *paccī* vā, *apacciṃsu*, *pacciṃsu*, *apaccuṃ*, *paccuṃ*. *Apacci*, *pacci*, *apacco*, *pacco* vā, *apaccittha*.
He cooked; we cooked, we cooked, we cooked, we cooked, we cooked, or we cooked.
He went to the village; they went; you went; you went; you went, you went, you went, or you went; you all went.
I went (*agacchiṃ*, *gacchiṃ*); we went (*mayaṃ agacchimha*, *gacchimha*, *agacchimhā*, or *gacchimhā*).
According to the rule beginning with “kvaci dhātū,” the substitute *ñcha* optionally replaces the *ccha* of the root *gam* in the present tense (*ajjatani*):
thus, *agañchi*, *gañchi*, *agañchī*, or *gañchī*; they went (*te agañchiṃsu*, *gañchiṃsu*, *agañchuṃ*, or *gañchuṃ*). You went (*tvaṃ agañchi*, *gañchi*).
Whether it be *agañcho*, *gañcho*, or *tumhe agañchittha*, *gañchittha*; [and] *ahaṃ agañchiṃ*, *gañchiṃ*, *mayaṃ agañchimha*, *gañchimha*, *agañchimhā*, or *gañchimhā*.
In the absence of the substitution of *ccha*, there are *so agami*, *gami*, *agamī*, or *gamī*—as in the rule: "In the present tense, the root *gam* becomes *kāsa*."

If it is said that for this stem *vada*, the substitution of *vajja* optionally occurs in all case endings (*vibhatti*). And here, because the context is the case endings, the phrase "in all" is established by implication.
The word "optionally" (*vā*) continues [from the previous rule]. 487. And the letter *a* of this [substitute] is elided.

The suffix *ap* following roots beginning with *bhū* undergoes the change to *ett*, and its elision (*lopa*) is optional. Here, because this is the section dealing with the rules for the formation of verbal suffixes (*vikaraṇa*), the suffix *ap* is understood as consisting of the vowel *a*.
Thus: "The suffix *ap* follows roots beginning with *bhū* and those beginning with *juhoti*;
it undergoes elision and no other [suffix does], according to the fixed rule of distribution (*vavatthitavibhāsā*)."
The *ekāra* (e) of a root (*appaccaya*) [is substituted], along with the elision of vowels (*saralopa*), and so forth; [the roots] *vajjeti*, *vadeti*, and *vadati* [are formed];
[and there is substitution] at the end—488. In certain instances, there are long vowels, contrary substitutions, elisions, and augmentations of verbal roots, case endings, and suffixes.

Here, in this section on verbal roots (*dhātu*) within the context of verbs (*ākhyāta*) and primary derivatives (*kitaka*), in certain applications where specific grammatical rules have not been prescribed, [these changes occur] for the roots.

The grammatical operations—namely, shortening, lengthening, reversal, substitution, elision, and augmentation—of these case endings and the suffixes prescribed for verbal roots occur in accordance with the words of the Victor (the Buddha). Among these:
"In the presence of the suffix *nām*, there is shortening of *ki* and so forth, as well as of other roots when followed by a consonant cluster."
In the case of the āyuṇa suffixes or the vibhatti endings, there is the shortening of the long vowel *ssānta*.

*vajjesi*, *vadesi*, *vadasi*; [second person plural: *vajjetha*, *vadetha*, *vadatha*. [First person singular: *vajjemi*, *vajjāmi*, *vademi*, *vadāmi*; [first person plural: *vajjema*, *vadema*, *vajjāma*, *vadāma*.

*vajje*, *vajjeyya*, *vade*, *vadeyya*, *vajjeyyuṃ*, *vadeyyuṃ*. *Vajjeyyāsi*, *vajjesi*, *vadeyyāsi*. *Avadi*, *vadi*, *vadiṃsu*.
*Vadissati*, *vadissanti*. *Avadissa*, and so forth. The root *kam* means "to step.

When the suffix *ap* is applied, there is doubling (*dvitta*) according to the rule: "In certain cases, single vowels such as *a* and others undergo doubling," and the *ka*-group is replaced by the *ca*-group.
The inclusion of *abbhāsa*, the inclusion of *anta*, and the inclusion of *vāk* are operative.

When *abbhāsa* occurs, there is optionally the augment (*āgama*) *niggahīta*. This word *vā* has the sense of a restricted option (*vavatthita-vibhāsa*); therefore, this [augment] applies only to *kama* and the others. Examples: *caṅkamati*, *caṅkamanti*, etc.; *kamati*, *kamanti*, etc.
In the sense of moving (*cala*): *kampane*, *cañcalati*, *calati*.
In the sense of breaking (*dalana*): *daddallati*.

Regarding the root *jhī* in the sense of meditating (*cintā*), by applying the rule "the vowel *e* [is substituted] for the vowel *a*" when there is no suffix, and by the analysis of the grammatical connection (*yogavibhāga*) in the rule "for *te* and *āvā*," even when not followed by a suffix, the substitution of *āy* for the vowel *e* occurs: *jhāyati*, *jhāyanti*, and so forth; this is a specific grammatical rule (*visesavidhāna*).

The method of the *tud-ādi* class [of verbs] does not undergo vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*). The root *tud* means "to strike" (*byathana*); from it, the suffix *a* arises as the *appaccaya*. Regarding the rule "and in other [cases]," the inclusion of the term *vāk* (speech) which is carried over (*anuvattita*) from that context serves as the specific distinction that the *tud-ādi* roots do not undergo vowel strengthening. Thus: *tudati*, *tudanti*; *tudasi*, *tudatha*; *tudāmi*, *tudāma*.

In the passive voice (*kamma*), according to the rule "for that [root], the *ca*-group [is replaced]," the letter *j* replaces the letter *s* of the *ya*-suffix, and doubling (*dvitta*) occurs: *tujjate*.
*tujjante*. *Tujjati*, *tujjanti*, or *tujjare*. Likewise: *tudatu*, *tudantu*; *tude*, *tudeyya*, *tudeyyuṃ*;

In the optative (kamme): *pavisiyyate*, *pavisiyyante*; *pavisiyyati*, *pavisiyyanti*; or *pavissate*. Likewise: *pavisatu*, *pavisantu*;

This is the *tudādi* class.

*Hū*: in the sense of existence (*sattāyaṃ*). From the root *bhū*, etc., there is the arising [of the suffix] by the rule "from *bhū* and so on, *a*" (*bhūvādito a*), which is the *ap*-suffix. With reference to the word "or" (*vā*), by the rule "and the elision of this *a*," there is the elision of the *ap*-suffix following roots such as *bhū*.
By the rule "and in other cases," there is vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*). Thus: *so hoti* (he is), *te honti* (they are). [In the second person singular: *hosi*, [in the second person plural:
*hotha*. [In the first person singular: *homī*, [in the first person plural: *homa*. In the impersonal sense (*bhāve*): *hūyate* (it is being).

"Let it be so," "let them be. [In] *hohi*, because the letter *a* follows, there is no elision of *hi*; thus, *hotha*. [First person singular: *homi*; [first person plural: *homa*. In the sense of the abstract action (*bhāve*), [the form is] *hūyate*.

In the seventh case (locative), following the rule for the elision of *sa* and so on: [second person singular] *heyya*, [second person plural] *heyyuṃ*. [Second person singular with suffix: *heyyāsi*, [second person plural: *heyyātha*. [First person singular: *heyyāmi*, [first person plural: *heyyāma*; or [with the suffix -yaṃ] *heyyaṃ*. In the sense of the abstract action, [the form is] *hūyetha*.

In the past tense (*hiyyattaniyaṃ*), after the elision of the suffix, by the rule beginning with "in some cases, of the root," there is the substitution of *uva* for the vowel *ū* of the root *hū*. [Thus: *ahuvā*.
*ahuvu*, *ahuvū*. *Ahuva*, *ahuvo*, *ahuvattha*. *Ahuvaṃ*, *ahuvamha*. *Ahuvattha*, *ahuvatthuṃ*. *A huvase*, *ahuvavhaṃ*. *Ahuviṃ*, *ahuvamhase*.

In the passive (*bhāve*), it is *ahūyittha*. In the present tense (*ajjatanimhi*), by the rule "kvaci dhātū" and so forth, there is the elision of the *ī* of the vibhatti and shortening [of the vowel] after *hū*; thus, with the elision, it is *so ahu*, and in the absence of elision:

In the expression “*karassa kāsattamajjatanimhī*,” here, by means of a grammatical split (*yogavibhāga*) of the rule "*sattamajjatanimhī*," there is the augment *s*, vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*), and [the forms] *ahosi*, *ahesuṃ*.
By the rule beginning with "*kvaci dhātū*," the long *o* becomes *e*. Alternatively, [there is the form] *ahavuṃ*. [The forms] *ahosi* and *ahosittha*. [The forms] *ahosiṃ* and *ahuṃ*;

here, there is elision of the following consonant (*parasara*) and shortening of the vowel. [The forms] *ahosimha* and *ahumha*; here, there is shortening of the vowel. In the sense of the abstract action (*bhāva*), [the form is] *ahūyittha*.
“*Hi lopaṃ vā*” (with elision of *hi*, or): from this point, “elision (*lopa*), or (*vā*)” also continues.
490. In the future tense (*bhavissantimhi*), the vowel of the root *hū* becomes *eha*, *oha*, or *etta*;
and there is optionally the elision of *ss*. There is the augment *ikāra* (the letter *i*), and the elision of the vowel, etc.
Hehiti, hehinti. Hehisi, hehitha. Hehāmi, hehāma. In the absence of elision (lopābhāve): hehissati, hehissanti.
Hehissasi, hehissatha. Hehissāmi, hehissāma. With the substitution of *o* (ohādesa): hohiti, hohinti. Hohisi, hohitha.
Hohāmi, hohāma. Likewise: hohissati, hohissanti. Hohissasi, hohissatha. Hohissāmi, hohissāma.
In the case of the substitution of *e* for *a*: *heti*, *henti*; *hesi*, *hetha*; *hemi*, *hema*; *hessati*, *hessanti*; *hessasi*, *hessatha*; *hessāmi*, *hessāma*.
In the passive (*bhāve*): *hūyissate*.
In the conditional (*kālātipatti*): *ahavissa*, *ahavissaṃsu*; *ahuyissatha*, etc.

*Hū*, *bhū*: in the sense of existence (*sattā*). Here, *bhū* is preceded by the prefix *anu*. There is the elision of the suffixes *ty-ādi* and *uppatti*, as well as the *vuddhi* (vowel strengthening).
[Thus: *anubhoti*, *anubhonti*. *Anubhosi*, *anubhotha*. *Anubhomi*, *anubhoma*. In the passive (*kamma*): *anubhūyati*, *anubhūyanti*.
Likewise: *anubhotu*, *anubhontu*. *Anubhohi*, *anubhotha*. *Anubhomi*, *anubhoma*. *Anubhūyatu*, *anubhūyantu*. [Optative: *anubhave*, *anubhaveyya*; *anubhūyeyya*. [Aorist: *anubhosi*.
*Anubhavi*. *Anubhossati*, *anubhossanti*. *Anubhossasi*, *anubhossatha*. *Anubhossāmi*, *anubhossāma*. Or *anubhavissati*.
*Anubhossa*, or *anubhavissa*, and so forth.
In the case of the root *sī* (to lie down), there is elision of the suffix and a vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*). Thus: *seti*, *senti*. *Sesi*, *setha*. *Semi*, *sema*. *Sete*, *sente*, and so forth.
In the absence of the elision of the *appa*-suffix, the term “before a vowel” (*sare*) applies, as does the mention of the verbal root (*dhātu*). 491.
*e* becomes *aya*.
When a vowel follows the final *e* of a verbal root, *ay* is substituted for it, with the elision of the vowel and so forth.

[Examples: *sayati*, *sayanti*; *sayasi*, *sayatha*; *sayāmi*, *sayāma*. In the passive (*kamma*), preceded by *ati*: by the rule “*kvaci dhātvā*” etc., when *yam* follows, the short vowel at the end of the root is lengthened: *atisīyate*, *atisīyante*. Also: *atisīyati*, *atisīyanti*.
In the impersonal (*bhāva*): *sīyate*. Likewise: *setu*, *sentu*; *sehi*, *setha*; *semi*, *sema*. [Imperative: *sayatu*, *sayantu*; *saya*, *sayāhi*, *sayatha*.

I lie down, we lie down. You lie down, you (plural) lie down. May you lie down, may you (plural) lie down. I lie down, we lie down (for ourselves). They lie down excessively, they lie down excessively.
Let them lie down excessively, let them lie down excessively.
In the passive: it is being lain down. I may lie down, he may lie down, they may lie down. He may lie down excessively. In the passive: it may be lain down.
*Asayi*, *sayi*, *asayimsu*, *sayimsu*, *asayum*. With the augment *ā* (*sāgame*), *atisesi*, *atisesum*. In the passive (*kamme*), *accasīyittha*, *accasīyi*, *atisīyi*.

In the impersonal (*bhāve*), *sīyittha*. [Future: *sayissati*, *sayissanti*. In the absence of the augment *i* (*ikārāgamābhāve*), *sessati*, *sessanti*. In the passive, *atisīyissatha*, *atisīyissati*.
In the impersonal, *sīyissate*. [Aorist: *asayissā*, *asayissaṃsu*. In the passive, *accasīyissatha*, and so forth.

The root *nī* means "to lead"; it is transitive (dvikammaka). Examples: *ajaṃ gāmaṃ neti*, *nenti* (he leads the goat to the village; they lead). *Nesi*, *netha*; *nemi*, *nema*. In the absence of elision (*lopābhāve*): *nayati*, *nayanti*, etc. In the passive (*kamme*):
*ajo devadattena gāmaṃ nīyate* (the goat is led to the village by Devadatta), *nīyare*, *nīyante*; *nīyati*, *nīyanti*. Likewise: *netu*, *nayatu*;
*nīyataṃ*, *nīyantaṃ*; *naye*, *nayeyya*; *nīyetha*, *nīyeyya*. *Anayi*, *nayi*, *anayiṃsu*, *nayiṃsu*; *vinesi*, *vinesuṃ*. *Anīyittha*, *nīyittha*. *Nayissati*, *nessati*; *nayissate*.
*nīyissate*, *nīyissati*. *Anayissa*, *anīyissa*, and so forth.
Regarding the root *ṭhā* in the sense of stopping or ceasing motion, the word "optionally" (*vā*) is understood to carry over. 492. *ṭhā-ṭhiṭṭho*.
The substitution of *tiṭṭha* optionally occurs for this root *ṭhā*. The word "optionally" (*vā*) here has the sense of a fixed alternative (*vavatthita-vibhāsa*).

There is the elision of the suffix. Thus: *tiṭṭhati*, *tiṭṭhanti*; *ṭhāti*, *ṭhanti*. When there is no elision, by the rule "in some cases [the augment] after a root," etc., the letter *h* is inserted after *ṭhā* and the vowel is shortened;
with the prefix *sam-*, it becomes *saṇṭhahati*, *saṇṭhahanti*. With the prefix *adhi-*, it becomes *adhiṭṭhāti*, *adhiṭṭhenti*.

**Kamme (The Passive Voice) – 493.** In the domain of the passive voice (*bhāvakamma*), when the suffix *ya* follows, there is the substitution of *i* for the roots *dā*, *dhā*, *mā*, *ṭhā*, *hā-pā*, *maha*, and *matha*, and so forth. [Note:
This rule applies to the formation of the passive verb stem by replacing the final vowel of these specific roots with *i* before the suffix *ya*.]
It undergoes the change to the vowel *ī* internally; this undertaking is for the sake of expressing permanence (*niccattha*). [Examples: *upaṭṭhīyati*, *upaṭṭhīyanti*.
With the addition of the letter *h* and the shortening of the vowel, there is the insertion of the vowel *ī*:
*patiṭṭhahīyati*, *patiṭṭhahīyanti*. In the sense of a state (*bhāva*): *ṭhīyate*. Likewise: *tiṭṭhatu*, *tiṭṭhantu*; *ṭhātu*, *ṭhantu*; *saṇṭhahatu*, *saṇṭhahantu*; *tiṭṭhe*, *tiṭṭheyya*.
*Saṇṭhe*, *saṇṭheyya*, *saṇṭheyyuṃ*. *Saṇṭhahe*, *saṇṭhaheyyuṃ*. *Aṭṭhāsi*, *aṭṭhaṃsu*. *Saṇṭhahi*, *saṇṭhahiṃsu*.
*Pakiṭṭhissati*, *patiṭṭhissanti*. *Ṭhassati*, *ṭhassanti*. *Patiṭṭhahissati*, *patiṭṭhahissanti*.
*Patiṭṭhissa*, *patiṭṭhissaṃsu*. *Patiṭṭhahissa*, *patiṭṭhahissaṃsu*, and so forth.
*Pā* means "to drink"; the word *vā* ("or") is understood [from the previous rule]. 494. *Pā* means "drink.
For this root *pā*, the substitution *piba* optionally occurs. This word *vā* has the sense of a restricted option (*vavatthita-vibhāsa*).
He drinks. Let him drink. He might drink. By the rule beginning with "kvaci dhātu-," the letter *ba* becomes *va*, resulting in *pivati*, *pivanti*.
Alternatively, *pāti*, *pānti*, or *panti*. [Passive: *pīyate*, *pīyante*; *pīyati*, *pīyanti*. Imperative: *pivatu*. Optative: *piveyya*. Aorist: *apāyi*, *pivi*.
Future: *pivissati*. Conditional: *apivissa*, and so forth.
In the case of *asa* on the earth, there is the arising of a case ending (*vibhattuppatti*) and the elision of the suffix (*appaccayalopa*).
Here, in the word *asa*, both “*asasmā*” and “elision of the final syllable” (*antalopa*) apply.
495. There is the state of *tissa*.

When, after this [word] *asaññī*, there is the presence of the third case ending (*tissa vibhatti*) for another word, there is elision of the final syllable of the stem. There is [the suffix] *atthi*.
The word "optionally" (*vā*) continues [from the previous rule]. 496. In all instances, there is also elision of the initial vowel (*assādi*) of the suffix.

In all cases, including among the case endings (*vibhatti-paccaya*), there is optionally the elision (*lopa*) of the initial [consonant] of this root; the word "optionally" (*vā*) here has the sense of a fixed alternative (*vavatthita-vibhāsa*).
The rule "from *asasmā*, there is elision of the final [consonant]" is also the governing heading (*adhikāra*). 497.
And in the locative singular (*simhi*).
The elision of the final vowel of the root *asa* occurs before the case ending *si*. [Thus: *tvaṃ asi*. 498.
The substitution of *ttha* for *tha*.
After this root *asa*, the following case ending *tha* becomes *ttha*, and there is also elision of the final vowel of the root. [Thus: *tumhe attha*.
The word "vā" (or) is understood [from the previous rule]. 499. *Asasmā mimānaṃ mhimhāntalopa ca*.

After the root *asa* (to be), for the case endings *mi*, *ma*, *iccetāsaṃ*, there are optionally the substitutes *mhi* and *mhā*; furthermore, there is elision of the final sound of the root. Thus: *amhi*, *amha*; *asmi*, *asma*.
500. *Tussa tthuttaṃ*.

When the suffix *tu* follows this root, it becomes *tthutta*, and there is elision of the final syllable of the root. Thus: *atthu*. There is also elision of *asassādi*: *santu*. With the suffix *āhi*: *attha*. With *asmi*: *asma*.

In the seventh case (*sattamī*), there is elision of *asassādi*; by the rule beginning with "kvaci dhātū," the suffixes *eyya* and *eyyuṃ* become *iyā* and *iyuṃ* respectively for the roots *as* and so on. Thus: *siyā*, *siyuṃ*.

In the absence of the elision (*lopābhāve*), by the rule "kvaci dhātvādi," there are substitutes *ssa*, *ssu*, *ssa*, *ssatha*, *ssaṃ*, and *ssāma* for the non-existent *eyya* and others, together with the end of the root.
Thus: *assa vacanīyo*, *assu*. *Assa*, *assatha*. *Assaṃ*, *assāma*.
In the past tense (*ajjataniye*), there is the augment *akāra* and lengthening: *āsi*, *āsiṃsu*, *āsuṃ*. *Āsi*, *āsittha*. *Āsiṃ*, *āsimha*.
The phrase “or, *asassā*” is also understood [to apply here]. 501. *Bhū* occurs in place of *assa* when followed by any suffix other than a verbal root (*dhātu*).

What is the purpose of [the root] *vāti*?

It is for the sake of speed (*āsuṃ*). In the case of *brū*, there is the substitution of *viyattiyaṃ* for *vācāyaṃ*, the arising of the suffix *tyādi*, and the elision of the *appaccaya*. The word “in some cases” (*kvaci*) is understood to carry over.
502. *Brū* with *ī*:

After the root *brū*, the augment *ī* is sometimes inserted before the third-person plural case-ending (*timhi*), subject to the rules for vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*), substitution (*āvādesā*), and the elision of vowels (*saralopādi*).
Thus, *bravīti* and *brūti*. By virtue of the extension of the term "vowel" (*vaggahaṇa*) from the rule *aññesu ca*, there is vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*) of the consonant following the root *brū*.
It does not exist. In the plural, by the rule “*jhalānam iyuvā sare vā*,” there is an optional substitution of *u* for the vowel *ū*; thus: *bruvanti*.
By the rule “*kvaci dhātvādīnaṃ*,” etc., there is optionally the substitution of *a*, *u*, or *ā* for the endings *-ti* and *-nti*, and the substitution of *āh* for *brū*;
thus: *āha*, *āhu*. *Brūsi*, *brūtha*. *Brūmi*, *brūma*. *Brūte*, *bruvante*. *Brūse*, *bruvavhe*. *Bruve*, *brūmhe*.
Brūtu, bruvantu; brūhi, brūtha; brūmi, brūma; brūtaṃ, bruvantaṃ; bruve, bruveyya, bruveyyuṃ; bruveyyāsi, bruveyyātha; bruveyyāmi, bruveyyāma;

bruveyya, bruveraṃ; abruvā, abruvū. Regarding the aorist (*parokkhā*): by the rule "In the aorist, *brū*, *bhū*, *namāha*, and *bhūvā* [take their substitutes]," there is the substitution of *āha* for the root *brū*;
with the elision of the vowel and so forth, it is said that in the case of "dreaming" (*supina*) it becomes *māha*. Therefore the ancients say: *āhaṃsu* and so on.

In the present tense (*ajjataniya*), [the forms] are *abravi*, *abruvi*, *abravuṃ*. In the future, *bravissati*. In the conditional, *abravissa*, and so forth. The root *hana* is used in the senses of harming and going.
When the suffix *ti* follows, there is sometimes the elision of the *ap*-suffix: *hanti*, *hanati*, *hananti*; *hanasi*, *hanatha*; *hanāmi*, *hanāma*.

In the passive voice, by the rule “*tassa cavagga*” etc., *ñ* is substituted and doubling occurs: *haññate*, *haññante*, *haññare*; *haññati*, *haññanti*. In the imperative: *hanatu*, *hanantu*. In the optative: *haneyya*.
The rule "hana" applies. 503.
Or "vadhā" everywhere:
for this root *hana*, there is a substitution of *vadha* in all case-suffixes; this is intended as a fixed alternative expression (*vavatthita-vibhāsa*).
The word *vā* [indicates an alternative]. *Vadheti*, *vadhiyati*; *vadhetu*, *vadhiyatu*; *vadheyya*. *Avadhi*, *avadhiṃsu*;

*ahani*, *ahaniṃsu*. *Vadhissati*, *hanissati*. In the case of the *khā* substitute: *paṭihaṅkhāmi*, *paṭihanissāmi*. *Avadhissa*, *ahanissa*, and so forth. This is the method for the root *hū* and others.

In the case of *hu*, *dāna*, *adāna*, and *abyappadāna*, there is the arising of *ty-ādi* and the suffix *ap*. In *kupa* (to be agitated), there are *kuppati* and *kuppanti*.

In *janajanane*, [the rule] “*janādīnamā timhi cā*” applies; here, by means of the grammatical split (*yogavibhāga*) “*janādīnamā*,” the vowel *ā* is substituted for the final letter of the roots beginning with *jan*.

Thus: *jāyati*, *jāyanti*; *jāyate*, *jāyante*. In the passive (*kamme*): *janīyati*, *janīyanti*. *Jāyatu*. *Jāyeyya*. *Ajāyi*, *ajani*. *Jāyissati*, *janissati*. *Ajāyissa*, *ajanissa*, and so forth. This belongs to the *divādigaṇa*.
In the *svādigaṇa*, the case endings arise as before, with the addition of *su*. 512.
After roots beginning with *svad*, the suffixes *ṇuṇ* and *āuṇ* [are applied].

Thus, from the group of roots beginning with *dhā*, these suffixes—*ṇu*, *ṇā*, and *ṇāi*—occur as agentive (*kattari*) case-suffixes prescribed for those [roots]. Regarding the phrase "and in others" (*aññesu ca*), by the inclusion of the word "and" (*ca*), there is vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*) for the suffix *ṇu*.
However, by the recurrence of the word "vowels" (*vā*) in that very same context, there is no strengthening for the vowels of the *svādi* group before the suffixes *ṇu*, *ṇā*, and so on.

He hears the Dhamma; [with the elision of *ra*] they hear. You hear, you two hear. I hear, we hear. With the suffix *ṇa*, he hears, they hear. You hear—by the rule beginning with “in some cases for roots,” there is shortening—[thus] *suṇasi*; you two hear, you all hear. I hear, we hear.

In the passive voice, with the suffix *ya*, by the rule beginning with “in some cases for roots,” there is lengthening: it is heard, they are heard. It is heard, they are heard. In the reduplicated form, there is shortening: it is being heard, they are being heard; or alternatively, *sūyyati*, *sūyyanti*.
Let him hear, let them hear. Hear thou, hear ye. I hear, we hear. Let him hear, let them hear. Hear! Hear thou!
Listen. (I) listen, (we) listen. (You two) listen, (you all) listen. (May you) listen, (may you) listen. (May I) listen, (may we) listen. In the passive:

(it is) being heard, (it is) being heard. (May it) be heard, (may they) be heard. (May I) listen, (may he) listen, (may they) listen. (May you) listen, (may you) listen. (May I) listen, (may we) listen. (May you two) listen, (may you all) listen. (May you two) listen, (may you all) listen. (May I) listen, (may we) listen. (It is) being heard, (it is) being heard.
Asuṇi, suṇi; asuṇiṃsu, suṇiṃsu. Asuṇi, asuṇittha. Asuṇim, suṇim; asuṇimha, suṇimha. Asuṇittha, suṇittha.
With the elision of the suffix *ṇa*, the substitution of the vowel *vuddhi* (guna), the doubling of the *s*, and the insertion of *s*, [the forms] are:
assosi, assosiṃsu, paccassosuṃ. Assosi, assosittha. Assosiṃ, assosimha, or assosimhā; assosittha. Asūyittha, assūyi.
*Saralopādi*: *suṇissati*, *suṇissanti*; *suṇissasi*, *suṇissatha*; *suṇissāmi*, *suṇissāma*; *suṇissate*, *suṇissante*;
*suṇissase*, *suṇissavhe*; *suṇissaṃ*, *suṇissāmhe*. With the elision of the suffix *-ṇa* and the substitution of the vowel *vṛddhi*, [we have]:
*sossati*, *sossanti*; *sossasi*, *sossatha*; *sossāmi*, *sossāma*; *sossate*. [In the passive: *sūyissate*, *sūyissati*. [Aorist: *asuṇissa*, *asūyissa*, and so forth.

In the sense of sending (*hi-gatimhi*), with the prefix *pa-* and the suffix *-ṇa*, we have: *pahiṇāti*, *pahiṇati* or *pahiṇanti*; *pahiṇātu*, *pahiṇantu*; *pahiṇeyya*; *pahiṇi*, as in "he sent a messenger" (*dūtaṃ pāhesi*); *pahiṇissati*; *pahiṇissa*, and so forth.
In the sense of covering (*saṃvaraṇe*), [from the root] *vu*: *āvuṇāti*, *āvuṇanti*, and so forth. In the sense of throwing (*pakkhepe*), [from the root] *mi*:
by the rule "in some cases, the suffix *ṇa* becomes *na*" (*kvaci dhātū* etc.), there is the substitution of *na* for *ṇa*: *minoti*, *minanti*, and so forth.

In *pāpuṇane*, because of the prefix *pa-* and the elision of the vowel *a* according to the rule "long [vowel] after *pa-," the vowel becomes long; the suffix *uṇ* is added. One attains success, they attain [it]. *Pāpuṇāsi*, *pāpuṇātha*. *Pāpuṇāmi*, *pāpuṇāma*. In the passive (*kamma*), *pāpīyati*, *pāpīyanti*.
Likewise, *pāpuṇātu*, *pāpīyatu*. *Pāpuṇe*, *pāpuṇeyya*. *Pāpīyeyya*. *Pāpuṇi*, *pāpuṇiṃsu*. *Pāpīyi*. *Pāpuṇissati*, *pāpīyissati*. *Pāpuṇissa*, *pāpīyissa*, and so forth.
*Saka* means "to be able. There is reduplication: *sakkuṇāti*, *sakkuṇanti*. In the abstract state (*bhāva*), by the rule "and the former form," there is the state of the former form.

It can be done by you, it is able to be done, or may it be able to be done. It might be able to be done (*sakkuneyya*). By the rule beginning with “*kvaci dhātū*,” there is the substitution of *khā* for the root *sak* in the present and other tenses:
he was able (*asakkhi*), he was able (*sakkhi*), they were able (*asakkhiṃsu*, *sakkhiṃsu*). He will be able (*sakkhissati*), they will be able (*sakkhissanti*).
He was unable (*asakkhissa*), they were unable (*asakkhissaṃsu*), and so forth.
The *svādi-gaṇa*.
The *kiyādi-gaṇa*:
the root *krī* is used in the sense of exchanging goods; when preceded by *vi*, it undergoes reduplication (*dvitta*), and case endings arise as before.

513. *Kiyā* etc.: From the verbal root *mā* onwards, the suffix *nā* occurs in the sense of the agent (*kattari*). Because it ends in *n*, there is no vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*). By the rule beginning with “*kvaci dhātū*,” the shortening of the vowels in *kiyā* etc. occurs before the suffix *nā*; furthermore, the letter *n* of the suffix *nā* becomes *ṇ*.
He sells the merchandise: *vikkīṇāti*, *vikkīṇanti*. It is sold: *vikkīyati*, *vikkīyanti*. Let him sell: *vikkīṇātu*, *vikkīṇantu*. Let it be sold: *vikkīyatu*.
Let them be sold. He sells, he would sell. It may be sold, they may be sold. He sold, he sold. It was sold, it was sold.
He will sell, they will sell. It will be sold, they will be sold. He did not sell, they did not sell. It was not sold, they were not sold.
It would have been sold, they would have been sold, and so forth.
*Ji*: he conquers; he overcomes the defilements (*kilesa*); they conquer. *Jīyati*, *jīyanti*: he is conquered; they are conquered. Likewise:
*jinātu*, *jīyatu*; *jineyya*, *jīyeyya*. *Ajini*, *jini*, *ajiniṃsu*, *jiniṃsu*; *ajesī*, *ajesuṃ*; *ajinittha*;
*ajīyittha*, *ajīyi*. *Jinissati*, *jinissanti*; *vijessati*, *vijessanti*; *jīyissati*, *jīyissanti*. *Ajinissa*, *ajīyissa*, and so forth.
Likewise, [the forms] *ciye*, *cināti*, *cinanti*, and so forth.
From the root *ñā* in the sense of "understanding," the suffix *nā* is applied. The word "or" (*vā*) is understood to carry over.
514. *Ñāssa jā jaṃ nā*:
For this element *ñā*, the substitutes *jā*, *jaṃ*, and *nā* optionally occur.
The substitute *jā* occurs in the locative singular (*nāmhi*), *jaṃ* in the locative plural (*ñāmhi*), and the absence of *nā* occurs in the instrumental plural (*timhi*) in this context.
The particle *vā* follows the meaning of the fixed analysis (*vavatthita-vibhāsa*). [Examples:
*dhammaṃ vijānāti*, *vināyati*, or *vijānanti*. In the passive (object) voice:

*viññāyati*, *viññāyanti*. With the addition of the vowel *i*, there is the elision of the preceding [consonant], and by the rule beginning with "in some cases, for roots," there is the substitution of *e* and doubling of the consonant.
*Ñeyyati*, *ñeyyanti*. *Vijānātu*, *vijānantu* (with shortening). *Vijāna*, *vijānāhi*, *vijānātha*. *Vijānāmi*, *vijānāma*.
*Vijānataṃ*, *vijānantaṃ*. *Vijānassu*. *Viññāyatu*, *viññāyantu*. 515.
For the suffix *eyya*, there are the substitutes *ñāto*, *iyā*, or *ñā*.
In place of the *ñā* of this case-ending (*vibhatti*), the substitutes *iyā* and *ñā* optionally occur after the root *vijānāti*, following the elision of the vowel (*saralopa*), etc.
[Thus: *vijāniyā*. When there is the substitute *ñā*, the substitute *jaṃ* occurs for that *ñā*. The phrase “*ñāto vā*” also continues [from the previous rule].
516. *Nāssa lopo yakārattaṃ*.

There is optionally the elision (*lopa*) of the suffix *nā* following this root *ñā*, and there is also the substitution of the letter *y*. This word "optionally" (*vā*) has the sense of a fixed distribution (*vavatthitavibhāsa*).
Therefore—when the suffix *ñā* follows, there is always the elision of *nā*.
In words such as *vibhāsā* and *jatanā*,
this [suffix] does not occur elsewhere; therefore,
there is no substitution of the letter *y* for *t* in the locative case (*timhi*).

One should know that the *niggahīta* (the nasal *m*) is the final member of a consonant group (*vagga*). One should know; one should know; they should know. You should know; you [plural] should know. I should know; we should know; or "we should know" (*vijānemu*). You [plural] should know.

It should be known; they should be known. They were born together; they were born; they were born. When there is no elision (*alopa*), he knew; they knew. He understood; they understood. It was understood;
they were understood. He will know; they will know. He will cognize; they will cognize. It will be cognized; it will be cognized by them.
*Paññāyissati*, *paññāyissanti*. By the rule beginning with “*kvaci dhātū*,” the suffix *-ss-* becomes *-hi-*, resulting in *paññāyihiti*, *paññāyihinti*.
*Ajānissa*, *ajānissatha*; *aññāyissatha*, *aññāyissa*, and so forth.
In the root *mā* (to measure), by the rule beginning with “*kvaci dhātū*,” the final *-mānta* becomes *-ikāra-*: *mināti*, *minanti*. In the passive (*kamma*), *mīyati*, *mīyanti*, and so forth.
*Lū* (to cut): with the *nā*-suffix, there is shortening; *lunāti*, *lunanti*; *lūyati*, *lūyanti*, and so forth.
*Dhū* (to shake): *dhunāti*, *dhunanti*; *dhūyati*, *dhūyanti*, and so forth.
*Gaha* (to take): when the *nā*-suffix is reached—
517. *Gahāditoppaṇhā*.
From roots beginning with *gaha* and so forth, the suffixes *ppa* and *ṇha* occur in the sense of the agent (*kattari*). This word *ādi* (beginning) signifies "manner" (*pakāra*).
The term "*gahassa*" is understood [from the previous rule].

518. *Halopo ṇhāmhi*. There is the elision (*lopa*) of the letter *ha* of the verbal root *gaṇh* when the suffix *ṇhāmhi* follows. [Examples: *sīlaṃ gaṇhāti*, or by shortening [the vowel], *gaṇhati*; [plural] *gaṇhanti*. [Second person singular] *gaṇhāsi*; [second person plural] *gaṇhātha*. [First person singular] *gaṇhāmi*; [first person plural] *gaṇhāma*.

In the passive voice (*kamme*), while the term "ye" is being discussed, there is a substitution (*pariyaya*) of the letter *ya* for the letter *ha* according to the rule "there is optionally a substitution of *la* for *ha*. [Examples: *gayhati*, *gayhanti*.
Let him take, let them take. Take, take thou, take ye. I take, we take. Let him be taken, let them be taken. He was taken, they were taken.
Let him be taken, let them be taken. May he take, may he take, may they take.
May he be taken, may they be taken. He took, he took; they took.
When, by the rule beginning with “kvaci dhātu,” there is the elision of the vikaraṇa suffix in non-sabbadhātuka [forms], and the substitution of *e* for the augment *i*, then that is the augment *s*.
*aggahesi*, *aggahesuṃ*; *aggahi*, *aggahiṃsu*, *aggahuṃ*. *aggayhittha*, *aggayhi*. *gaṇhissati*, *gaṇhissanti*.
*gahessati*, *gahessanti*. *gahīyissate*, *gahīyissante*. *gayhissati*, *gayhissanti*.
Aggaṇhissa, aggahissa; aggaṇhissatha, aggahissatha; aggayhissatha, aggayhissa, and so forth. Regarding the *ppa* affix:
519. *Gahassa ghe ppe*. (The substitution of *gha* for *gaha* occurs before the *ppa* affix.)
The substitute *gha* occurs for this root *gah* before the suffix *ppa*. Examples include *gheppati*, etc.
[This concludes] the *kiyādi* group. [Now begins] the *tanādi* group.
*Tanu* means "in expansion. As in the previous [section], there is the elision of the final phoneme of the root and the arising of case endings (*vibhatti*).
520. *Oyira* follows *tanu* and so forth.
From the group of roots beginning with *tanu*, these suffixes—namely *oyira*—are applied in the sense of the agent (*kattari*). Indeed, this suffix *yira* is a substitute for *ka*.
He extends the Dhamma; they extend it. You extend it; you (plural) extend it. I extend it; we extend it. The word “or” (vā) is understood [from the previous rule].
521. The vowel *o* is the highest.
From the root *tan*, the suffix *o* optionally becomes the highest (the first person singular). This word "optionally" (*vā*) has the sense of a fixed alternative (*vavatthitavibhāsa*).

And here, because this is the section on the rules for the formation of verbal suffixes (*vikaraṇa*), the suffix *o* is understood as the suffix *ov*. [Thus: *tanute*; in the plural, according to the rule "and *ya* and *ā*," it is *tanvante*.
[In the first person singular: *tanuse*; [in the first person plural: *tanuvhe*. [In the middle voice first person singular: *tanve*; [in the middle voice first person plural: *tanumhe*.

In the *Kammatthāna* [manual], according to the rule beginning with "in some cases, the root" (*kvaci dhātū*), for a root ending in *-tanu*, when the letter *a* occurs before the suffix *ya*, the forms are *patāyate* and *patāyante*.
Without the letter *a*, they are *pataññati* and *pataññanti*. The optative forms are *tanotu* and *tanontu*;
*taneyya* and *taneyyuṃ*. The aorist forms are *atani* and *ataniṃsu*; *atāyittha* and *patāyi*. The future forms are *tanissati* and *tanissanti*; *patāyissati* and *patāyissanti*.
*Atanissa*. *Patāyissa*, and so forth.
In the sense of "doing" (*karaṇe*), as in "he performs merit" (*puññaṃ karoti*).
When the plural number is indicated by the rule "optionally" (*vā*), and the suffix *utta* is applied, [it becomes] *uttamokāra*.
The phrase “or, *utta*” is understood [to apply here].

522. And the substitution of *a* for *kara*. For this root *kara*, the letter *a* optionally becomes the final vowel (*uttama*). This word *vā* has the sense of a restricted option (*vavatthita-vibhāsa*).
Regarding the rule *“yavakārā ca”* (and after *ya* and *va*, [the vowel] *o* becomes *va*):
for a root ending in *u* (such as *ku*), the *u* is changed to *va* by the rule *“kvaci dhātū”* etc.; when the *va* is doubled, that *va* becomes two *ba*s according to the rule *“bbo vvassā”*;
thus: *kubbanti*, *karonti*. *Karosi*, *karotha*. *Karomi*, *karoma*. Likewise: *kurute*, *kubbante*. *Kuruse*, *kuruvhe*. *Kubbe*.
We perform (*kurumhe*). By means of the *ya* suffix, there is the elision of the letter *ra*, as in *kayirati*, *kayiranti*, and so forth.
When the passive *ya* suffix is applied, by the rule "the vowel *ī* is optionally inserted after a palatal (*ivaṇṇa*)," the vowel *ī* is inserted, and the letter *ya* is doubled:

*karīyyate* (the mat is being made by him), *karīyyati*, *karīyyanti*. Or alternatively, *karīyati*, *karīyanti*. In the absence of the vowel *ī*, by the rule beginning with "for that [root], the *ca*-group [is substituted]," etc.
The substitution of *y* for the final *dh* of a verbal root (*dhātu*) occurs, as does doubling (*dvitta*). Thus: *kayyati*, *kayyanti*.
When there is the insertion of *i* (the augment), according to the rule beginning with “*kvaci dhātu*,” etc., the doubling of *r* and *y* is optionally reversed by the inclusion of the particle *ca*;

thus: *kayirati kaṭo tena*, *kayiranti*, and so forth. Likewise: *kusalaṃ karotu*, or *kurutu*, *kubbantu*, *karontu*. *Karohi*, *karotha*. *Karomi*, *karoma*. *Kurutaṃ*, *kubbantaṃ*. *Kurussu*, or *kurassu*, *kuruvho*. *Kubbe*, *kubbāmase*.
In the present tense: *karīyatu*, *karīyantu*, *kayyataṃ*, *kayirataṃ*, *kayiratu*.

In the optative (*sattamī*): *kare*, *kareyya*, *kareyyuṃ*; *kareyyāsi*, *kareyyātha*; *kareyyāmi*, *kareyyāma*. In the *utte* suffix: *kubbe*, *kubbeyya*. In the *yir* affix: [the forms are as follows].
In the case of *yirato āttameyyassa*, as in *ethādisseyyum* and similar forms, there is the elision of the suffix *eyya* by means of the rule beginning with "kvaci dhātū.
Following the elision of *sa* and so forth, we have *kayirā* and *kayiruṃ*. [The forms] *kayirāsi*, *kayirātha*, *kayirāmi*, and *kayirāma* follow. [This concludes the section on] the *attanopada*.

In the sense of "one should do," one may say *kayirātha*, *kubbetha*, or *karetha*; by the rule "in some cases [the root] *dhātu* [becomes *kr*]," etc., the *kru* of *kus* is substituted, resulting in *krubbetha*, *krubberaṃ*.
[The forms] *krubbetho*, *krubbeyyāvho*; *krubbeyyaṃ*, *krubbeyyāmhe* [are likewise formed]. In the passive voice, [one says] *karīyeyya*, *karīyeyyuṃ*.
In the past tense (*hiyyattaniya*), by the analysis of the rule (*yogavibhāga*) "for *kara*, *kā* [is substituted]," *kā* occurs, with the elision of the vowel and so forth.
Aka, akarā, akarū. Akaro, akattha, akarottha. Akaṃ, akaraṃ, akamha, akaramha. Akattha. Akariṃ, akaramhase. The word “vā” (or) is understood [from the previous rule].
523. The root *kar* becomes *kās* in the present tense.
When any following present tense suffix (*ajjatanī-vibhatti*) follows, the substitution of *kā* for the root *kar-* occurs, and there is the augment *satt*.
By this description as a verbal derivative (*bhāva-niddesa*), this augment is added after other roots as well.

Alternatively, the meaning is that when *kā* replaces *kar-* and the augment *satt* is added in the present tense, then—by means of a grammatical split (*yogavibhāga*) of the rule "in the seventh [case] and in the present tense"—it applies to other roots as well.

The form *sāgamopi* is established from the root (*dhātu*). Because of the rule "the desired [form] is established through the analysis of the grammatical connection" (*yogavibhāga*), it generally occurs with a long vowel.
Furthermore, by the analysis of the connection "for *kara*, [substitute] *kā*," the substitution of *kā* is established for the past tense (*hiyyattaniya*).
Thus: *akāsi*, *akāsuṃ*; *akāsi*, *akāsittha*; *akāsiṃ*, *akāsimha*; *akāsittha*. In the absence of the suffix *kāsatta*, it is *akari*.
*kari*, *akariṃsu*, *kariṃsu*, *akaṃsu*, *akaruṃ*. *Akari*, *akarittha*. *Akariṃ*, *kariṃ*, *akarimha*, *karimha*.
*Akarittha*. *Akarīyittha* or *akarīyi*. The rule "or, there is elision of the *ss* of the future tense" (*vā, lopo, bhavissantimhi ssassa*) also applies here.
524. *Kara* with its suffix becomes *kāha*.
For this root *kara*, when accompanied by a suffix, there is optionally the substitution of *kāha* in the future tense (*bhavissanti*), and there is the elision of *ss*.

By the inclusion of "accompanied by a suffix" (*sappaccaya*) and "that which has already occurred" (*adhikabhūta*), there is the substitution of *khā* for *ss* in [roots] such as *vaca*, *muc*, and *bhuja*; [as in] *vasa* (to cut).
There is also a substitution (*chādeso*) for the [root] beginning with *labh*.
[Examples: *kāhati*, *kāhanti*; *kāhasi*, *kāhatha*; *kāhāmi*, *kāhāma*. With the addition of the vowel *i* (*ikārāgame*), there are forms such as *kāhiti*, *kāhinti*, and so forth.
In the absence of *kāhi*, there are *karissati*, *karissanti*; *karissasi*, *karissatha*; *karissāmi*, *karissāma*; and *karissate*.
*karissante*. *Karissase*, *karissavhe*. *Karissaṃ*, *karissāmhe*. *Karīyissati*, *karīyissanti*.
*Akarissa*. *Akarīyissā*, and so forth.

When preceded by a prefix (*saṃpubba*), then by the rule "In the case of *karoti* preceded by *purā*, *sam*, *upa*, or *pari*, there is the substitution of *kha* for [the initial *ka*] when followed by a consonant (*khara*)," through the division of the grammatical rule (*yogavibhāga*), there is the substitution of *kha* for the initial of *karoti* even in the *tyādi* case endings when it is preceded by a prefix.
*Abhisaṅkharoti*, *abhisaṅkharonti*. *Abhisaṅkharīyati*, *abhisaṅkharīyanti*. *Abhisaṅkharotu*. *Abhisaṅkhareyya*.
*Abhisaṅkhari*, or *abhisaṅkhāsi* in the aorist. *Abhisaṅkharissati*. *Abhisaṅkharissa*, and so forth.
The suffix *-saka* occurs in the sense of ability (*satti*). *Sakkoti*, *sakkonti*. *Sakkosi*, *sakkotha*. *Sakkomi*, *sakkoma*, and so forth.
Regarding *pāpuṇati*: with the prefix *pa-*, [it becomes] *pappoti*, *papponti*; *papposi*, *pappotha*; *pappomi*, *pappoma*; *pappotu*, *pappontu*, and so forth. This belongs to the *tanādigaṇa*.
Now, the *curādigaṇa*.
In *dhura* and *theyye*, there is elision of the internal vowel (*dhātvantalopa*) as in *pure*, followed by the arising of the case ending (*vibhattuppatti*).

From the rule *“tathā kattari ca”* (and likewise in the agent), by means of a "lion's glance" (*sīhavilokana*), the terms *kattari* (in the agent) and the references to the abstract state (*bhāva*) and the object (*kamma*) continue to apply; furthermore, by means of a "frog-leap" (*maṇḍūkagati*), the reference to the causative (*kārita*) also applies. 525. After roots beginning with *cur*, the suffixes *ṇa*, *ṇaya*, and *ṇeyya* [are applied].

Thus, from the group of roots beginning with *cura*, these suffixes—*ṇa* and *ṇaya*—occur in the sense of the agent, as well as in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāva*) and the passive (*kamma*), among the case-suffixes. According to the rule “the *kārita* [suffix] is like *ṇa*,” the designation *kārita* is applied to *ṇa* and *ṇaya*.
526. Elision of *ṇ* after *kārita* suffixes:
the letter *ṇ* undergoes elision after *kārita* suffixes.
527. There is *vṛddhi* for a root ending in a non-conjunct consonant when followed by a *kārita* suffix.
Since there is *vṛddhi* for a root ending in a non-conjunct consonant when a *kārita* suffix follows, the *u* of the root becomes *o*, which is the *vṛddhi*.
[Examples: *dhanaṃ coreti*, *corenti*; *coresi*, *coretha*; *coremi*, *corema*. With the *ṇaya* suffix: *corayati*.
They steal. You steal. You (plural) steal. I steal. We steal. He steals for himself. They steal for themselves. You steal for yourself. You (plural) steal for yourselves.
I steal for myself. We steal for ourselves.

When the *ya*-suffix occurs in the passive voice, there is the insertion of the vowel *ī*, along with the elision of the *s* and *r*, and so forth: *corīyate* by Devadatta, *corīyati*, *corīyanti*, and so on.
He steals, he steals. Let him steal. He may steal, let them steal. Steal, steal thou!
He might steal, they might steal. He would steal, they would steal. He stole, he stole; they stole, they stole. He caused to steal, he caused to steal;
they caused to steal, they caused to steal; they caused to steal, they caused to steal. He stole, he stole. You caused to steal.
*acorayittha*. *acoresiṃ*, *acoresimha*. *acorayiṃ*, *acorayimha*. *acorayittha*. *acorīyittha*, *acorīyi*. *corissati*, *corissanti*.

*corayissati*, *corayissanti*. *corīyissate*, *corīyissante*. *corīyissati*, *corīyissanti*. *acorissa*, *acorayissa*. *acorīyissatha*, *acorīyissa*, and so forth. Likewise for *cinta* (to think): *cintāyaṃ*;
because it ends in a conjunct consonant, the absence of vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*) is the only distinction.

*Cinteti*, *cintayati*, *cintenti*, *cintayanti*. *Cintetu*, *cintayatu*. *Cinteyya*, *cintayeyya*. *Acintesi*, *cintesī*, *acintayi*, *cintayi*. *Cintessati*, *cintayissati*. *Acintissa*, *acintayissa*, and so forth.
*Manta* (in the sense of "speaking secretly"): *manteti*, *mantayati*, and so forth, similar to the preceding [root]. *Pāla* (in the sense of "protecting"):
*dhammaṃ pāleti*, *pālayati*. *Pālīyati*. *Pāletu*, *pālayatu*, and so forth.
*Ghaṭ* in the sense of "joining": *ghaṭate*, *ghāṭeti*, *ghāṭayati*, *ghaṭeti*, *ghaṭayati*; there is optionally an increase (*vuddhi*) [of the vowel] for roots beginning with *ghaṭ*.
*Vid* in the sense of "knowing": *vedeti*, *vedayati*. *Gaṇ* in the sense of "counting":
by the rule "optionally for roots beginning with *ghaṭ*," there is no increase; thus *gaṇeti*, *gaṇayati*, and so forth. All of this is easily understood.
The *cur-ādi* class.
The *bhū-ādi*, the *rudh-ādi*, the *div-ādi*, and the *sv-ādi* classes;
the *kry-ādi*, the *tan-ādi*, and the *cur-ādi*—thus there are seven classes here.
The exposition of the vikaraṇas is completed.
Now, the method regarding verbal roots, suffixes, and endings is stated. First, the verbal roots, suffixes, and endings are explained.
In this context, those suffixes beginning with *khādi* that have been demonstrated as having the sense of verbal roots (*dhātu*) are called *dhātuppaccaya*.
[The rule] "the designation *dhātu* applies to *tija*, *nisāna*, *bandhana*, and *khamā*" follows from the previous section.

From the statement "suffixes following the verbal roots (*dhātuliṅga*)", the mention of "verbal roots" (*dhātu*) is carried over from here, and "following (*parā*), suffixes (*paccayā*)" is the governing heading.
528. *Tija-gupa-kita-mānehi kha cha sā vā*.
After the verbal roots *tija*, *gupa*, *kita*, and *māna*, the suffixes *kha*, *cha*, and *sa* optionally follow.
From *tija*, *kha* is used in the sense of patience (*khanti*); from *gupa*, however, *cha* is used in the sense of reproach (*nindā*).
The *kit* suffix is added after a word ending in a vowel, provided it is a distinct term (*vavatthita*) or a verbal root (*vibhāsa*).
Regarding the rule "the doubling of single initial consonants," this refers to the doubling of the first consonant of a verbal root (*dhātu-ādi*).
While the condition "after a final consonant" (*byañjanantassa*) is being observed—
529. *Ko khe ca*.
When the suffix *kha* follows, there is a substitution of the letter *k* for a final consonant of a verbal root.
Thus, when *titikkha* is established—
He states that the case endings beginning with *ty* do not occur after what is not a verbal root (*adhātu*).
530. Case Endings from Roots and Suffixes:

When the meaning of a root has been indicated by suffixes such as *khādi*, *kārita*, and *ta*, the case endings beginning with *ty* occur; as before, [the tenses] such as the present (*vattamāna*) and so forth are to be applied.

He endures harsh speech; they endure it. He is made to endure the task. Likewise: may he endure, may they endure. He should endure, they should endure. He endured, they endured. He will endure. "He would have endured," and so forth. In the absence of the *kh* suffix, the vowel *e* replaces the zero-suffix (*appaccaya*):
*tejeti*, *tejati*, or *tejanti*, and so forth. The root *gup* (to protect) takes the suffix *cha*;
there is reduplication (*dvibhāva*), and by the rule "the first part is the *abbhāsa*," the technical term *abbhāsa* is applied. While the rule "of the *abbhāsa*" is in effect...
“*Antassivaṇṇākāro vā*” means that for the *abbhāsa* (the original form) *s*, there is *t*; and for the *abbhāsa* *g* of *kavaggassa cavaggo*, there is *j*. 531. *Byañjanantassa co chappaccayesu ca*:

For a consonant at the end of a verbal root (*dhātu*), there is the substitution of the letter *c* when the six suffixes follow. Then [follow] the case-endings (*vibhattiyo*): *kāyaṃ jigucchati*, *jigucchanti*. The rest is the same as before. When *cha* is absent: *gopeti*, *gopenti*, etc.
In the case of *rogāpanayana*, there are six conditions and two taddhita suffixes.
The inclusion of the prefix *abhi-* applies as well. 532.
Or, for those who are proud, there is the state of being so (*vatatta*).
In the case of these verbal roots *māna*, *kita*, etc., which have reached the *abbhāsagata* stage, there is optionally the substitution of *va* or *ta*.
Accordingly, there is *ta* for the final consonant of the root, and *ca* for the penultimate consonant; the rest is the same. For example: *tikicchati*, *tikicchanti*, etc.
In the absence of *ta*, there is *ca* according to the rule "the *ca*-group replaces the *ka*-group," as in: *vicikicchati*, *vicikicchanti*, etc.
In the case of *māna*, *vīmaṃsā*, and *pūjā*, there are the substitutions of *dv*, *bhā*, *īkāra*,
and *vakāra* when followed by an affix (533).
Thereafter, after *pāmā* or *māna*, or after roots (*dhātu*), the substitutions *vāmaṃ* occur respectively when followed by an affix due to proximity (*abbhāsato*).

*Pare*. The designation *sesu* as a plural form is intended to indicate that even in actual usage there may be a transposition of number (vacana-vipallāsa), as in *atthaṃ vīmaṃsati* or *vīmaṃsanti*, and so forth.
Elsewhere, according to the rule *“lopañcettamakāro”* [Kacc 640], the suffix *a* is elided and replaced by *i*, as in *māneti* and *mānenti*.
The root *bhuja* is used in the senses of protecting (*pālana*) and dealing/trading (*byavaharaṇa*); in the sense of desiring to enjoy (*bhottum icchati*), it forms [the verb *bhujeti*].
The suffixes *kha*, *cha*, and *sa* are also applied.
(534) After the verbal roots *bhuja*, *ghasa*, *hara*, *su*, and *pā*,
when followed by the infinitive suffix *tum* or the sixth case ending (*ṣaṣṭhī*), these suffixes— namely *kha*, *cha*, *sa*, and so forth— are applied.

Or they exist. The meanings of *tum* and of desire joined with *tum* are the meanings of *tum-iccha*; therefore, [the suffixes] do not occur in cases where *tum* has been elided, such as in "desires food" (*bhojanamicchati*).
Or, because of the rule "there is no employment of that which has already expressed its meaning," there is no employment of the sentence.

When the doubling of the root-initial and so forth has been performed, according to the rule "for the second and fourth [consonants], the first and third [are substituted]," the letter *ba* replaces the repeated letter *bha*. [This applies to] the end of the root...
“*Ko khe cā*” means the letter *ka*. [Examples: *bubhukkhati*, *bubhukkhanti*, etc.
Why is *vā* used? [To indicate that the suffix is optional: *bhottumicchati*. Why is *icchatthesu* used? [To show it applies when meaning "to wish"]: *bhottuṃ gacchati*.

In the sense of “eating” (*ghasa adane*), when the meaning is “he wishes to eat,” the suffix *cha* is applied; there is doubling of the consonant (*dvittaṃ*); the third letter of the *ca*-group (*ca*) and the vowel *i* undergo substitution for the letter *ca*; thus: *jighacchati*, *jighacchanti*.
In the sense of "taking" (*haraṇe*) or "desiring to take" (*haritum icchati*), [the root *hṛ*] is with its suffixes.
535. *Harassa gī se*.

For this root *hara*, *gī* replaces the whole [root] before the suffix *se*. By the analysis of the rule (*yogavibhāgena*), *gī* applies to both *jī*; and because the designation "root" (*dhātuvohāra*) applies to the substitute (*ādesa*) by metonymy of position (*ṭhānūpacārena*), there is doubling (*dvitta*). Thus: *bhikkhaṃ jigīsati*, *jigīsanti*.
In *su-savaṇe* (in the sense of hearing): one who wishes to hear is *sussūsati* or *sussūsanti*; the long vowel [of the suffix] occurs by the rule beginning with "kvaci dhātū. In *pā* (to drink):

in the sense of wishing to drink, there is the substitution of the suffix *sa*, the doubling of the consonant, and the replacement of the short vowel with *i*; then, by the rule "tato pāmānānaṃ vāmaṃ sesū," there is the substitution of *vāma*;
thus: *pivāsati*, *pivāsanti*, and so forth. In *ji* (to conquer): one who wishes to conquer is *vijigīsati*, and so forth.
The meaning is: "The Saṅgha conducts itself like a mountain," or "it conducts itself as if it were a mountain.
536. *Āya* is a suffix added after a noun denoting the agent of comparison, in the sense of conduct (*ācāra*).
The suffix *āya* occurs after a noun that serves as the standard of comparison for the agent of the action of conducting oneself, in the sense of conduct. It is compared [to that].

By this [term], *upamāna* (simile) is meant; *kattūpamāna* is the simile of the agent. By the rule "there is no employment [of the suffix] when the meaning has already been expressed," the word *iva* is excluded.
Because they consist of roots and suffixes, the elision of case-endings occurs by the inclusion of the term "those" in the sutta "the case-endings of those [roots and suffixes] are elided.

By the rule "and its base [remains] when it ends in a vowel," the state of being the base (*pakati*) is established, resulting in the elision of vowels and so forth. [The case-endings are added] by the rule "case-endings [are added] after roots and suffixes."
The arising of case endings: *saṅgho pabbatāyati* (the Saṅgha acts like a mountain); likewise, one behaves toward oneself as if toward the ocean, thus *samuddāyati*;
one behaves toward oneself as if making the sound *cicciṭ*, thus the sound is *cicciṭāyati*. In this way, one "smokes" (*dhūmāyati*).
And the phrase "in the sense of name, in the sense of behavior" continues [to apply].
537. *Īyūpamānā ca*.

The suffix *īya* arises after a word that functions as a standard of comparison (*upamāna*) in the sense of conduct (*ācāra*). The repetition of the term "standard of comparison" is for the purpose of excluding the agent (*kartṛ*);

therefore, it is also established after the object (*kamma*). The rest is the same [as the previous rule]. One behaves like one who has no umbrella; he acts as if he were an umbrella: *chattīyati*. One who has no son...
The teacher behaves toward the pupil as toward a son; thus, *puttīyati* (he treats as a son).
Why [is it] "comparison"? [Example: he practices the Dhamma. Why "practice" (*ācāra*)? [Example: he protects one without a parasol as if with a parasol.
The term "*īya*" is understood [to follow].
538. *Nāmamhātticchatthe*.

After a noun, the suffix *īya* occurs in the sense of "desiring for oneself. One desires a bowl for oneself: *pattīyati*; likewise, *vatthīyati*, *parikkhārīyati*, *cīvarīyati*, *paṭīyati*, *dhanīyati*, *puttīyati*. Why is it said "in the sense of desiring for oneself"?
[To show that] one desires another's bowl [does not take this suffix].
In the sense of “he makes firm his energy,” the suffix *kāritagga* (causative) is understood to follow;
[this occurs] from a noun before a verbal root, with the addition of the suffix *ṇa*. 539.
[This applies] to the form of the root after a noun, and also with the suffix *ṇa*.

When a material form (rūpa) is to be produced from a root (dhātu), or when [words] such as "he makes that" or "he surpasses by means of that" are to be employed, the suffix *ṇa* occurs after a noun, and it is designated as having the sense of agency (*kārita*).
When the suffix *ṇa* is elided, and after the elision of case-endings (*vibhatti*) and the elision of the *sar* augment have been performed, the case-ending arises:
*daḷhayati vīriyaṃ* (he strengthens his energy), likewise *pamāṇayati*, *amissayati*, and similarly with *hatthinā*.
*Atikkamati* becomes *atihatthayati*; *upagāyati* becomes *upavīṇayati* (plays the lute); *visuddhā hoti* becomes *visuddhayati*;
*kusalaṃ pucchati* becomes *kusalayati*, and so forth. 540.
The causative suffixes *ṇe*, *ṇaya*, *ṇāpe*, and *ṇāpayā* are added to verbal roots (*dhātu*) in the sense of motive (*hetvatthe*).
After all roots (*dhātu*), when the sense of cause (*hetvattha*) is to be expressed, the suffixes *ṇe*, *ṇayaṇāpe*, and *ṇāpaya* are added; these are designated as *kārita*.

The "sense of cause" (*hetvattha*) is simply the meaning of cause; and that which causes another to act receives the designation "cause" (*hetu*) according to the rule "he who causes [another] to act is the cause.

This refers to the instigator of the pure agent (*suddhakattā*), whose causal agency consists, in actual fact, of the instigating activity of directing or requesting. In this context, "cause" (*hetu*) means such an instigating operation.
And here: "The suffixes beginning with *ṇ* are introduced after [a stem ending in] *ā*; the last two may be doubled;
after the remainder, four or two [suffixes are introduced], following the recurrence of the word 'or' (*vā*)."
Roots are intransitive (without an object), but when used in the causative sense they become transitive (with an object).
Those that are transitive may have two objects, and those with two objects may even have three.
Therefore, the occurrence of the causative verb form arises from both the agent and the object.
In the passive construction (*kārita*), that which is designated as the object (*kamma*) is [the same as] the pure agent (*suddhakattā*) in the active sense (*bhāve*);
for verbs beginning with *ni*, the primary [agent] is [the object], while for verbs beginning with *duh*, the non-primary [agent] is [the object].
In the passive, both the pure agent and [the non-primary agent] are called the "object" within the domain of the verb (*ākhyātagocara*).
In this context, anyone who exists is addressed by another as "be! be! (*bhavāhi bhavāhi*);
or else, one impels someone capable of being, or in the sense of "impels [him] to be," the suffix *ṇe* is applied by the rule of *ṇeṇayappaccayā*, and it is designated as a *kārita* (causative).

Furthermore, according to the rule "there is non-application of that which has already expressed its meaning" (*vuttatthānamappayogo*), there is non-application of the verbal root; and according to the rule "there is elision of *ṇ* after *kārita* suffixes" (*kāritānaṃ ṇo lopo*), the *ṇ* is dropped.
There is elision of the *ṇ*. According to the rule “*asaṃyogantassa vuddhi kārite*,” there is the vowel-increment (*vuddhi*) of the letter *ū* to *o*.

The terms “*o*” and “*e*” are understood [from the previous rule], as is the mention of the verbal root (*dhātu*). 541. Those two, *ā* and *āv*, [occur] when a suffix with the marker *K* (*kārita*) follows.
Those *okāra* and *ekāra* vowels that have become part of the verbal root (*dhātu*) undergo substitution with *āva* and *āya* when a *kārita* suffix follows.

By means of a rule-splitting (*yogavibhāga*) stating "those [substitutions] are *āva* and *āya*," they occur even after roots such as *jhe* when not followed by a *kārita* suffix; thus there is the substitution of *āva* for the *okāra*, the elision of the vowel (*saralopa*), and so forth, and then the case-endings (*vibhatti*) such as *ti* and others arise according to the rule "case-endings [follow] from roots and suffixes.

He develops concentration: *bhāveti*, *bhāvayati*; they develop: *bhāventi*, *bhāvayanti*. You developed: *bhāvesi*, *bhāvayasi*; you two developed: *bhāvetha*, *bhāvayatha*. I develop: *bhāvemi*, *bhāvayāmi*; we develop: *bhāvema*, *bhāvayāma*. He develops (for himself): *bhāvayate*; they develop (for themselves): *bhāvayante*.

In the passive voice (*kamme*), there is the addition of the augment *i* due to the condition of the word beginning with a vowel (*attanopadāyappaccaya-ikārāgama*), as well as the elision of the vowel *a* (*saralopādi*).

Thus: *bhāvīyate*, *bhāvīyante*; *bhāvīyati*, *bhāvīyanti*. Likewise: *bhāvetu*, *bhāvayatu*; *bhāventu*, *bhāvayantu*. *Bhāvehi*, *bhāvaya*, *bhāvayāhi*; *bhāvetha*, *bhāvayatha*. *Bhāvemi*, *bhāvayāmi*; *bhāvema*, *bhāvayāma*.
*Bhāvayataṃ*, *bhāvayantaṃ*. In the passive: *bhāvīyataṃ*, *bhāvīyatu*, *bhāvīyantu*.
He would develop; he might develop; he should develop. They would develop; they might develop. You would develop; you might develop.
You (plural) would develop; you might develop. I would develop; I might develop. We would develop; we might develop.
May you develop; may you develop. May you (plural) develop; may you develop.
One should cultivate; they should cultivate.

In the form *ajjataniyaṃ*, there is the addition of the long vowel *ā* after the *s* due to the rule of grammatical splitting (*yogavibhāga*) stating "in the seventh [case] from today" (*sattamajjatanimhi*).
[The forms are: *abhāvesi*, *bhāvesi*; *abhāvayi*, *bhāvayi*; *abhāvesuṃ*, *bhāvesuṃ*; *abhāvayiṃsu*, *bhāvayiṃsu*.
abhāvuṃ, bhāvuṃ. abhāvesi, abhāvayasi, abhāvittha, abhāvayittha.
abhāvesiṃ, bhāvesiṃ, abhāvayiṃ, bhāvayiṃ, abhāvimha, abhāvayimha.
In the passive: abhāvīyittha, abhāvīyi.
Bhāvessati, bhāvayissati, bhāvessanti, bhāvayissanti. Bhāvessasi, bhāvayissasi, bhāvissatha, bhāvayissatha. Bhāvessāmi, bhāvayissāmi, bhāvessāma, bhāvayissāma.
In the passive (kamma): bhāvīyissate, bhāvīyissante. Bhāvīyissati, bhāvīyissanti. Aorist:
abhāvissa, abhāvayissa, abhāvissaṃsu, abhāvayissaṃsu. In the passive: abhāvīyissatha, abhāvīyissa, and so forth.

Likewise, when someone is cooking and another says to him, "Cook! Cook! (*pacāhi pacāhi*), or when one causes another who is cooking to cook, or causes another to be employed for the purpose of cooking—in these senses, the suffixes *ṇe*, *ṇaya*, and so forth are applied according to the method already stated.
The vowel *a* is changed to *ā* as a *vuddhi* (strengthening) substitute; the rest is to be understood accordingly. He causes Devadatta to cook rice: *pāceti*, *pācenti*;
*pācesi*, *pācetha*; *pācemi*, *pācema*. [In the causative] *pācayati*, *pācayanti*; *pācayasi*, *pācayatha*; *pācayāmi*, *pācayāma*. But in the cases of *ṇāpeti* and *ṇāpayati*, that man...
